Notes.Text:
This update for perl-Data-Dump-Streamer fixes the following issues:

Changes in perl-Data-Dump-Streamer:

Updated to 3.1.0 (3.001):

See /usr/share/doc/packages/perl-Data-Dump-Streamer/Changes

3.001 - 2026-11-10:

- Perltidy source to my preferred format. Fixed issues serializing
  the global stash. Added test to detect if serializing the global
  stash breaks anything.
- Fix version assignments so PAUSE can index the distribution.

3.00 - 2026-11-10:

- Rewrite the dumping engine in C/XS, with AI assistance, for improved speed,
  correctness and compatibility with Perl's refcounted stack. Improve Unicode
  and regexp handling, and add experimental support for XPerl class objects.
  (CVE-2026-126673 bsc#1290113)

- Require Perl 5.18 or newer and a C compiler. Replace Module::Build with
  ExtUtils::MakeMaker.

- There is no pure-Perl version. Please don't upgrade if you need pure-Perl
  support.

- Normalize CPAN version
  See https://github.com/openSUSE/cpanspec/issues/47 for details

Vulnerabilities.Description:
Data::Dump::Streamer versions before 3.00 for Perl allow code injection via unescaped Regexp patterns in _dump_qr.

A Regexp's pattern is written into a qr literal without escaping "$" or "@", so "@{[ ... ]}" and "${\ ... }" in the pattern run as code when the dump is evaluated. An already escaped delimiter gets a second backslash, which leaves the delimiter bare and ends the qr literal early.

An attacker who supplies a pattern that an application compiles, dumps and later restores with eval or do can run arbitrary Perl code.
